name: Clear floors and walkways
description: Keep walkways open. Loose rugs, cords, and clutter are easy to trip on.
intendedUse: Reduce trip hazards at home
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.

name: Bright, even lighting
description: Use bright light in halls, stairs, and bathrooms, including at night.
intendedUse: Make walking paths easier to see
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.

name: Bathroom steadiness
description: A shower seat, grab bars, and a non-slip surface are common supports. Placement and install matter.
intendedUse: Steadier bathing and toileting
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.

name: Eating and kitchen aids overview
description: Built-up or weighted utensils, and items kept within easy reach, can make meals simpler when hands shake or feel stiff.
intendedUse: Eating and kitchen tasks
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Assistive Tech Devices page, paraphrased.

name: Dressing aids overview
description: Button hooks, sock aids, and simpler clothing can reduce fine-motor strain while dressing.
intendedUse: Getting dressed
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Assistive Tech Devices page, paraphrased.

name: Walking aids overview
description: Canes and walkers are options to discuss with a physical therapist. Fit and training matter more than the brand.
intendedUse: Walking support to discuss with a therapist
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Assistive Tech Devices page, paraphrased.

name: Reach and bending overview
description: Keeping everyday items at arm level, and using a reacher, can cut down on stretching and rushing.
intendedUse: Reduce reaching and rushing
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.

name: Weighted spoon
description: A single spoon with a little extra weight. Some people find that steadier for tremor.
intendedUse: Eating when hands shake
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Weighted utensil set
description: A small set of weighted utensils. Higher example price than a single spoon.
intendedUse: Eating when hands shake
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Button hook
description: A simple hook that can pull a button through a hole.
intendedUse: Fastening buttons
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Dressing aid kit
description: A bundled example with a button hook, sock aid, and long shoehorn.
intendedUse: Getting dressed with less fine-motor strain
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Reacher
description: A short grabber for light items on the floor or a shelf.
intendedUse: Pick up light items without bending far
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Long-handle reacher
description: A longer grabber. Higher example price than a basic reacher.
intendedUse: Pick up light items from a bit farther away
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Night lights (2 pack)
description: Two small lights for a hall or bathroom path at night.
intendedUse: See the path during night trips
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Non-slip bath mat
description: A mat with a grip backing for the bathroom floor.
intendedUse: Reduce slipping on a wet floor
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Adjustable cane
description: A basic cane example. Height should be set with a therapist, not guessed.
intendedUse: A walking aid to discuss with a therapist
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Rolling walker
description: A walker with wheels. This is a higher-priced example, not a prescription.
intendedUse: More walking support to discuss with a therapist
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Grab bar
description: A bar for a bathroom wall. It must be mounted into a solid support.
intendedUse: Something to hold during bathing or toileting
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Shower chair
description: A seat for the shower. A higher-priced example than a grab bar.
intendedUse: Sit while bathing
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.

name: Bed rail
description: A rail that may help with turning or standing from bed. Fit and entrapment risk need a clinician's review.
intendedUse: Bed mobility to discuss with a clinician
safetyNotes: The price is an estimate, not a store quote. Ask a therapist before buying or installing anything.
source: ParkCare equipment listings. Not a product endorsement.
